prerequisites: Knowledge of the symbols, specific graphics, electrical diagrams.

learning_outcomes.text: Adequate application of knowledge on energy conversion, electromagnetic and mechanical phenomena specific to static, electromechanical converters, electrical equipment, and electromechanical drives
Familiarize students with the study and usefulness of equipment used in lighting systems, respectively in welding.
Students have the opportunity to get acquainted with various lighting and welding installations, learn practical skills in their construction, sizing, operation, and maintenance.
Provide future engineers with practical skills in the design, construction, research, operation, repair, and maintenance of lighting and welding installations.

Project content
Chapter I. Interior lighting systems and conditions for achieving a comfortable light microclimate
Chapter II. Optimal lighting solutions used in structural and civil engineering.
Chapter III. Sizing of interior lighting installations.
Chapter IV. Lighting system design. Conclusions
Presentation of the project theme. Getting started with electrical lighting installations
Assignment of initial design data. Norms, guides, and related technical prescriptions
Establishing the conditions imposed on the electrical lighting installation. Choosing the type of source
Photometric calculation by the use factor method. Sizing of the interior lighting installation
Quantitative and qualitative checks. Point-by-point calculation
Sizing of the outdoor lighting installation of the building
Plan and scheme of the electrical lighting installation
Circuit sizing and choice of protection and switching devices
Checking of the solution obtained by using dedicated software (DIALUX, ELBALUX, PHILIPS LIGHTING etc.)
Final evaluation of the project
teaching_methods: Discussions on how to write the project
Explanations on choosing optimal lighting solutions
Presentation of circuit sizing methods and choice of protection and switching devices
Presentation of checking methods and lighting quality conditions
assessment_rules: To pass the exam, all subjects in the course must be treated to at least grade 5 standards. All laboratory works must be performed to be allowed to take part in the exam. The project must respect the format imposed by the elaboration procedure and the obtained results must be close to the real ones for a grade of 6, and elaborated to maximum standards for a grade of 10. The minimum performance standard involves designing components of a low complexity electrical system, developing and testing an electrical system analysis program, and solving problems specific to electrical installations with correct assessment of workload, resources, and risks.
